doc.title: Dick Katz interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002

title: Founding Milestone and the Helen Merrill albums
summary: Starting Milestone with Orrin Keepnews and the albums made with Helen Merrill in the 60s and 1980.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: that was — but anyhow Helen and I started rehearsing and about this time I didn’t know Orrin Keepnews that well. But, and he’s not that accessible a person until you get to know him. He’s not a “hail fellow well met” like — he’s very much an individual and he can have a dour, but he’s a great, great man but he’s not somebody going to slap you on the back say how you doing you know. So we ran into each other, our sons went to the same school. So Father’s Day I ran into him up there. We got to talking and he was going through this spectacular bankruptcy of Riverside Records. And he was about to be out of a job. And he was over qualified, trying to get a job, when he went to all these companies he would get letters saying you’re too qualified for a job like this and we don’t have a job upstairs. So he was having a hard time. So I had always had a thing in the back of my mind I’d like to try my hand at producing records, I had a lot of ideas. Some of it came from John, he had so many ideas about how to make records and stuff. And so what I did is I went to my brother-in-law and borrowed $10,000 and we started this little label called Milestone. Can you imagine? And to make a long story short we made some really nice records. Now meantime I had borrowed money, Helen and I wanted to do this record. And we had rehearsed all this stuff and we picked out all these songs and I wrote these charts and I hired Thad Jones and Jim Hall and Ron Carter and Pete LaRoca and myself. And we went in and did this. I hired, George Avakian did it for no money hardly, we made these tapes and they came out great, and we tried to sell them, nobody wanted them. Can you imagine? So when we started Milestone that was one of the first records we put out. Then five stars.

Oh yeah. And I’m very proud of that record. And then we made a sequel in 1968. By then Milestone is up and running and she made a deal with Japanese Victor, they owned the tape — no she owns the tape but they had the rights for America, or some kind of complicated deal. And we did that one with the same cast except Elvin Jones played the drums and I added Hubert Laws and I also made those charts. Then we made a third record in 1980 was it or ’79 for another label called — a now defunct label called Inner City but it had another life in Japan and came back out here, and that’s called “Chasing the Bird” and that’s with Pepper. It’s all Gershwin. And Pepper Adams and Joe Puma, Mel Lewis and Rufus Reid. So she sang these Gershwins and I also made the charts on that. Where two of the tracks, like one she sings “I Got Rhythm” straight and we played “Chasing the Bird” behind her, and then she sang “Embraceable You” and we’d play “Quassimodo.” So those three records I’m very proud of, particularly the first two.
